Balder, the god of light, beauty, and goodness—the most beloved of all the Aesir. He is the brightest of the gods, associated with light, purity, and beauty, and his mere presence dispels darkness. He is the son of Odin and Frigg, cherished by all gods and giants alike. In fact, he is the only being in all the nine worlds without cause to hate him.

His mother Frigg, fearing his death, bound all things with a solemn oath to spare him from harm. But the mistletoe plant was overlooked as too young and harmless to bother with. This tiny omission would prove fatal. Loki, the trickster, discovered this loophole and tricked the blind god Hod into wielding a mistletoe dart. When Hod threw it, the dart found Balder and killed him. His death is irreversible even by the gods' power. Frigg sent a messenger to the realm of death seeking his return, but he cannot leave until Ragnarok itself.

The grief of the gods runs so deep that all things weep for Balder's loss. This weeping became the origin of tears in the world. His death represents the tragic lesson that beauty and goodness offer no protection against fate and treachery. The gods mourn him profoundly, including his father Odin who grieves his passing deeply. His brother Thor also mourns with all the Aesir. Loki's manipulation of Hod shattered the peace of the gods and broke the bonds that held them together. And though the Norns, the weavers of fate, foresaw his death, their power could not be unmade, not even to save the brightest of the gods.
